faq.q: How are steel frame buildings built?
faq.a: Foundations go in first, then steel columns and beams are craned in and bolted into a grid, floor by floor. Concrete floors are poured on steel decking, and the outer walls are hung on last.
asks: Steps to build a steel building

faq.q: What do the columns do in a steel frame?
faq.a: Columns are the vertical members that carry every floor's weight down to the foundations. They are joined end to end so each column line runs from bottom to top.

faq.q: How are steel beams joined to columns?
faq.a: With high-strength bolts through steel plates, or by welding. Some joints are made stiff to resist sway, while simpler joints rely on separate diagonal bracing.
A curtain wall is a light outer skin, often glass and aluminium, that hangs from the floors like a curtain. It keeps out wind and rain but carries only its own weight.
asks: Why don't skyscraper walls hold it up?
Why are skyscrapers covered in glass?

faq.q: Why use steel for tall buildings?
faq.a: Steel is strong in both tension and compression, so slim columns and beams can carry big loads. Parts are made in a factory and bolted together quickly on site.
asks: Why are skyscrapers made of steel?

facts: The Home Insurance Building in Chicago, completed in 1885, is often called the first skyscraper because a metal frame carried much of its weight.
In a steel-framed building the outer walls carry little more than their own weight; the frame carries the floors.
